def main():
    import sys
    input = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(input[0])
    s = input[1]

    max_len = 0
    # We'll use dynamic programming where dp[i][j] represents the maximum journey length ending at position i with the substring s[j..i]
    # To optimize space, we'll use a 2D array where rows represent the end position and columns represent the start position
    # Initialize dp table
    dp = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]

    for length in range(1, n + 1):
        for i in range(n):
            j = i - length + 1
            if j < 0:
                continue
            current_sub = s[j:i+1]
            # The maximum journey length ending at i with substring s[j..i] is at least 1 (the substring itself)
            dp[i][j] = 1
            # Check all possible substrings of current_sub that are strictly shorter and appear before in s
            for k in range(j, i):
                sub = s[k:i+1]
                if len(sub) < len(current_sub) and sub in current_sub:
                    # The journey can be extended by the substring s[k..i]
                    if dp[k-1][j] + 1 > dp[i][j]:
                        dp[i][j] = dp[k-1][j] + 1
            # Also check if the current_sub can be part of a longer journey by extending previous substrings
            for k in range(j):
                if s[k:i+1] == current_sub:
                    if dp[k-1][j] + 1 > dp[i][j]:
                        dp[i][j] = dp[k-1][j] + 1
            # Update the global maximum
            if dp[i][j] > max_len:
                max_len = dp[i][j]

    print(max_len)

main()
